## Data Source
This dataset provides us with data from two main sources:CDC Wonder and KFF (Kaiser Family Foundation). The CDC wonder datasets provide mortality and population data , while the KFF datasets provide state-level Medicare and Medicaid data. The information from this lists all states , along with their income and medicare and medicaid use defend the notion of increasing healthcare spending in certain states. Five useful data elements would be State,Population,Mortality/Deaths,Medicare/Medicaid Spending and income. Data elements State/Character, Population/Numeric, Deaths/numeric, Medicare spending/numeric, income/numeric.Data elements State/Character, Population/Numeric, Deaths/numeric, Medicare spending/numeric, income/numeric


```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)


library(readr)
library(dplyr)

cdc_wonder_mortality <- read_csv("cdc_wonder_mortality.csv")
cdc_wonder_population <- read_csv("cdc_wonder_population.csv")
kff_cms_medicaid_state_summary <- read_csv("kff_cms_medicaid_state_summary.csv")
kff_cms_medicare_state_summary <- read_csv("kff_cms_medicare_state_summary.csv")
```

```{r}
medicare_clean <- kff_cms_medicare_state_summary %>%
  select(
    State = Location,
    Enrollees = `Total Traditional Medicare Part A and/or Part B Enrollees`,
    Spending = `Total Medicare Part A and/or Part B Program Payments`
  )
```

```{r}
head(medicare_clean)
```

```{r}
medicare_clean <- medicare_clean %>%
  mutate(Spending = readr::parse_number(as.character(Spending)))
```

```{r}
str(medicare_clean)
```

```{r}
head(kff_cms_medicare_state_summary, 2)
head(kff_cms_medicare_state_summary[[4]])
```

```{r}
medicare_clean <- medicare_clean %>%
  mutate(
    spending_per_enrollee = Spending / Enrollees
  )

head(medicare_clean)
```

```{r}
medicare_clean <- medicare_clean %>%
  filter(State != "UNITED STATES")

nrow(medicare_clean)
colSums(is.na(medicare_clean))
```

```{r}
write.csv(medicare_clean,
          "medicare_clean.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)
```
